rule: Typed receivers (decision A ...): a receiver whose type is given by a declaration — local, parameter, field/property (including ... `obj.field` chains whose property has a declared type), catch parameter, for-loop variable, pattern binding — or by `= new T(...)` gives `T#m` (high if defined in the scan, else medium). ... Body-less member declarations of scanned types are defined in the scan (high)
notes: call_type convention (SPEC names the six call_types but does not define direct vs method): a call with no written receiver is direct; a call with a written receiver (obj., this., super., a type or object name) is method; a class-name call `T(..)` that resolves to a constructor, and `: this(..)` / `: super(..)` / a supertype-list call, are constructor. Kotlin has no `new`; a `val x = T(..)` constructor call is treated as decision A's `= new T(...)`. 5-6: `local` is declared Shape (declared type wins over the Circle initializer); `param` is a Shape parameter; Shape#area is a body-less interface member of a scanned type, so high and in nodes (Decisions 2026-11-09, C1). 7-8: `val c = Circle(1.0)` types c as Circle. 9: constructor property `primary` declared Shape. 10: `holder.inner` is an obj.field chain whose property `inner` is declared Shape in Holder. 12: for-loop variable over List<Shape>. `class Circle(..) : Shape` names an interface in the supertype list: no constructor edge (an interface has no constructor). `+=`/`*` on Double are not calls.
